RECORDED IN THE ORIENT. EXCLUSIVELY FOR JAPAN AIR LINE

The special charm of JAL today began years ago.
From childhood, Japanese girls live in a world of
subtle delights. A tinkling wind bell seems to cool
a hot summer day. The lazy plock, plock of water
dripping into a bamboo pond can transform an
entry hall into a shaded mountain glen.
This awareness of beauty-even in the least of
things-is as natural to the hostesses of Japan Air
Lines as their desire to please honored guests.
This is the secret of JAL's unique service.
You feel it the moment you step aboard your JAL
Jet Courier. You see it in the "raked sand" carpet-
ing and traditional brocade motifs. You hear it in
the softly muted voice of vour kimono-clad host-
ess as she welcomes you aboard: "Irasshaimase."
You experience it as delightful JAL hostesses
attend your every wish. It is the special charm
of IAL todav.
Tsukiko-a study in classic grace.
JAL hostess Tsukiko kneels beside her koto, the
13-string Japanese harp, on a woven floor of rush-
scented tatami mats. For many years, she has
studied not only the techniques of the koto, but
its traditions.
2004 161. 002
For example, Tsukiko belongs to the Ikuta School
of Koto, and she plays her instrument while
kneeling at an angle to it. The Yamada School,
on the other hand, requires that the player kneel
facing it. And there is a centuries-old debate be-
tween the two schools as to which position is the
most esthetic; which "design"
of artist, instru-
ment, and music is most pleasing to behold.
This careful attention to the smallest detail of
Japanese tradition guides Tsukiko's life-whether
studying koto or gracefully pouring you a tiny
cup of warmed sake aboard the let Couriers of
Japan Air Lines. It is this devotion to pleasing
others that makes your JAL flight a truly unique
travel experience.
The two worlds of Noriko.
Japan Air Lines hostess Noriko poses in front of
the traditional pine tree of classic Noh theatre.
Starkly simple, Noh dancing is performed on
a nearly empty stage. A white cloth on a stick
represents a boat, a few steps means a long jour-
ney, an upturned face is joy, a downturned face
is sorrow. There is a world of meaning in the
sparest of movement and gesture-and each is
carefully practiced until it becomes instinctive
and natural.
Like the children (below right) depicting monks
of the 19th century Edo Period, Noriko's school-
ing included the study of classical Japanese
dance. And, like the leotard-clad girls (below
left), she also studied the more modern forms of
dance as well as the
arts and customs of
the West.
This harmonious
melding of East and
West gives Noriko
the cultivated back-
ground that enables her and her sister hostesses
to bring you JAL'S
unique interpretation
of perfect airline ser-
vice. Savor it in the
pampering attentions
of your hostess as she
offers the traditional
graces of Japan in the relaxing comfort of your
modern DC-8 JAL Jet Courier.
Enjoy the pleasures of the Orient
the world around on Japan Air Lines.
Ask your travel agent about "the
calm beauty of Japan at almost
the speed of sound."
